title: Operator handback and custodian rollforward playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the operator handback process for private Redwood deployments (VPC and on-prem variants) and provides a prescriptive rollforward (safe redeploy) and rollback procedure for common stateful and stateless failure modes. It is written for on-call operators, SREs, and customer custodian teams who will accept operational responsibility after initial deployment or vendor handoff.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Tenant-level and control-plane handback; post-installation verification; emergency rollback and controlled rollforward procedures for model-serving runtime and associated services (ingress, KV cache, telemetry gateway, edge bridge).
- Audience: Redwood field operations, customer platform operators, SREs, and solutions engineers.

Key objectives:
- Ensure a safe, auditable operator handback from deployment to customer custodian.
- Reduce mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR) for common regressions with a tested rollback path.
- Provide a conservative rollforward strategy to restore capacity with minimal customer impact.

Prerequisites (must be satisfied before handback):
1) Acceptance tests: all smoke tests in the Customer Acceptance Test Suite pass (latency, inference correctness, auth, telemetry).
2) Observability: dashboards for per-route latency, token throughput, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit-rate are configured and visible to custodians.
3) Access: custodians have least-privilege access to the control-plane operator role, redwoodctl, and read-only access to deployment audit logs.
4) Backups: configuration snapshots (Helm values / deployment manifests) and persistent state backups (KV cache snapshot if exported) are stored in the agreed S3-compatible bucket and verified via checksum.
5) Rollback images and artifacts: previous stable service images and model artifacts are available in the image registry with signed tags (example: registry.redwood.internal/models/model-v2026-11-01-signed).

Operator handback checklist (step-by-step):
1) Pre-handoff meeting (30–60 min)
   - Participants: Redwood field PM, deployment engineer, customer custodian lead, SRE on-call.
   - Agenda: acceptance test summary, outstanding tickets, maintenance windows, emergency contacts, and escalation matrix.
2) Shared artifacts and access transfer
   - Provide: deployment manifests, Helm charts, redwoodctl client config, KMS/HSM integration notes, and audit-log retention policy.
   - Verify: custodian can run redwoodctl auth whoami and read primary dashboards.
3) Observability walkthrough
   - Show dashboards: per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), per-model token rate, KV cache hit-rate, GPU temp and power, pod restart rate.
   - On-call playbooks: link to runbooks and sample alerts.
4) Telemetry and alerting validation
   - Fire a synthetic request and confirm ingestion end-to-end in tracing and logs.
   - Confirm PagerDuty/Slack channels are subscribed and test alerting integration (non-page test event).
5) Acceptance signature and formal handback
   - Custodian signs handback form (template provided in Appendix A).
   - Change ownership in the internal registry for on-call rotation and runbook ownership.

Rollbacks: triggers, isolation, and safe revert steps
- Rollback triggers (examples): sustained error-rate > 2% for 10m, P99 latency over SLO by 50% for 5m, KV cache eviction storms causing >20% tail latency spikes, or failed canary stage beyond rollback threshold.
- Quick isolation (1–5 min):
  1) Redirect traffic: use ingress route weight shift to fallback model or control-plane failover lane. Example: redwoodctl traffic set-weight --route chat-prod --model model-stable --weight 100
  2) Put canaries into quarantine: scale down canary replicas to 0 or cordon nodes running new images.
  3) Increase log and trace retention for the incident window.
- Full rollback (15–60+ min):
  1) Validate artifact availability: confirm stable image tag exists and signature checks.
     - Command: docker pull registry.redwood.internal/service:stable-2026-10-12 && cosign verify registry.redwood.internal/service:stable-2026-10-12
  2) Roll back control-plane/operator components first (non-disruptive): apply Helm values rollback for control-plane and confirm readiness.
     - kubectl apply -f manifests/control-plane-stable.yaml
  3) Stateful runtime rollback: perform model artifact swap with KV cache compatibility check. If the new model changed KV cache layout, perform a cache invalidation prior to revert: redwoodctl cache invalidate --tenant-id TID
  4) Redeploy previous model image and scale to pre-incident target using deployment automation: helm rollback <release> <revision> or kubectl set image deployment/model-serving model=registry...:stable-2026-10-12
  5) Re-run smoke tests and gradually re-open traffic (weighted traffic increase over 10–30 min).
  6) Create incident postmortem and attach evidence (traces, root-cause) to the rollback record.

Notes on stateful rollback nuances:
- KV cache migration backwards-incompatible changes: if model vN+1 modified KV key layout, a rollback may require a cold cache flush. Expect higher latency until warmed (documented SLA impact).
- Persistent volume migrations: if a migration was applied, rolling back may need data migration scripts to reverse or use snapshot restore; do not attempt with partial snapshots.

Rollforward (safe redeploy) strategy
- Use rollforward when rollback is not feasible (e.g., tolerable degradations, data migrations already committed, or security patches required).
- Principles: small increments, verification gates, and canary promotable milestones.
- Steps:
  1) Branch fix: apply minimal remediation to the image or configuration that addresses root-cause. Tag as hotfix and push: registry...:hotfix-2026-11-02.
  2) Canary rollout: deploy hotfix to a small slice (1–5% traffic or 1 node) for 10–30 minutes with increased observability and synthetic monitoring.
  3) Verification gates: automated smoke tests + manual operator sign-off. Gate metrics: error rate delta < 0.1%, P99 latency within SLO +10%.
  4) Progressive percentage ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with a minimum 10–30 minute observation window between steps.
  5) If at any gate trigger detected, abort and revert to previous stable image using the rollback procedure.

Automated runbook snippets (examples)
- Verify current traffic split:
  - redwoodctl traffic list --route chat-prod
- Force traffic to fallback model immediately:
  - redwoodctl traffic set-weight --route chat-prod --model model-fallback --weight 100 --expires 1h
- Snapshot current deployment manifests:
  - kubectl get deploy --namespace redwood -o yaml > deploy-snapshot-$(date +%F).yaml
- Promote a canary image after verification:
  - helm upgrade model-serving ./charts/model-serving --set image.tag=hotfix-2026-11-02

Escalation and ownership matrix
- Primary operator (custodian on-call): first 15 minutes - attempt isolation and traffic shift.
- Redwood SRE escalation: beyond 15 minutes or if rollback requires control-plane change. Redwood contact: SRE PagerDuty team (link provided in onboarding pack).
- Security escalation: if incident indicates data exposure, follow security incident response playbook and notify security@redwood.com.

SLOs and operational thresholds (for handback acceptance):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% for control-plane endpoints (monthly).
- Latency SLO: P50 < 20ms, P95 < 150ms for short chat requests (<512 tokens).
- Error budget policy: error rate >2% for 1 calendar day triggers incident review and prioritized rollback.

Appendix A — Handback signature template (copy/paste)
- Deployment ID: ________
- Customer custodian lead: ________
- Date of acceptance: ________
- Items acknowledged: observability, access, backups, rollback artifacts, runbooks
- Signature (custodian): ________

Appendix B — Communication templates
- Incident start (Slack/PagerDuty): "Incident: <brief> — activated at <time>. Current action: traffic shifted to fallback. On-call: <name>. See runbook: <link>."
- Post-incident customer summary: 1) What happened, 2) What we did (rollback/rollforward), 3) Impact and duration, 4) Next steps and remediation plan.

Appendix C — Related pages and artifacts
- private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 (onboarding checklist)
- private-deploy-operator-handshake-and-runtime-guardrails-2026 (runtime guardrails)
- operator-driven-immutable-deployments-reference-2026 (reference architecture)

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: engineering (private deployments team).
- Review cadence: semi-annual or after any production rollback event.
